jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Senior Environmental Scientist to support environmental compliance, permitting, regulatory strategy, environmental due diligence, and project execution for clients throughout the Midwestern United States.

The successful candidate will lead and support environmental compliance programs, permitting initiatives, regulatory coordination, and environmental due diligence efforts across a diverse portfolio of projects within the energy, mining, construction, industrial manufacturing, transportation, utilities, and infrastructure sectors.

This position requires a strong understanding of federal, state, and local environmental regulations, permitting processes, and environmental compliance programs. The ideal candidate will collaborate closely with clients, regulatory agencies, engineers, planners, contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams to develop practical compliance solutions, obtain regulatory approvals, manage environmental risk, and support successful project delivery.

Your Impact

Lead and support environmental compliance programs for operational and construction-phase projects.
Develop and implement environmental compliance strategies supporting project development, construction, operations, and facility expansions.
Interpret and apply federal, state, and local environmental regulations, permit requirements, and environmental commitments.
Conduct compliance audits, inspections, and gap assessments to identify regulatory risks, deficiencies, and corrective actions.
Track permit obligations, environmental commitments, reporting requirements, and compliance deadlines.
Support the development and implementation of environmental management systems, standard operating procedures, compliance plans, and tracking programs.
Prepare and support environmental permit applications and regulatory approvals involving agencies such as the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), U.S.
nvironmental Protection Agency (EPA), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), state environmental and natural resource agencies, and county and local regulatory authorities.
Develop permitting strategies that align regulatory requirements with project schedules and client objectives.
Coordinate environmental permit approvals, agency consultations, and regulatory review processes.
Support environmental reviews for energy, mining, industrial, construction, transportation, utility, and infrastructure projects.
Conduct and/or oversee wetland delineations, aquatic resource assessments, threatened and endangered species evaluations, ecological reconnaissance surveys, environmental constraints analyses, site assessments, environmental screening studies, construction compliance monitoring, and reclamation and restoration planning.
Interpret environmental data and prepare technical reports supporting permitting, compliance, and regulatory consultation activities.
Evaluate environmental risks and provide practical, technically sound recommendations to support project implementation.
Lead and support environmental due diligence activities associated with acquisitions, divestitures, property transactions, financing activities, and project development opportunities.
Evaluate environmental liabilities, regulatory compliance risks, permitting constraints, and other environmental considerations associated with project sites.
Support environmental reviews under applicable federal, state, and local regulatory frameworks, including the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and applicable state environmental review requirements.
Identify environmental constraints and permitting risks early in project development and recommend appropriate avoidance, minimization, and mitigation strategies.
Coordinate multidisciplinary environmental reviews involving natural resources, hazardous materials, cultural resources, land use, and regulatory considerations.
Prepare due diligence reports, environmental review documentation, technical memoranda, and other environmental deliverables for clients, lenders, investors, and project stakeholders.
Support siting studies, alternatives analyses, and environmental feasibility assessments for energy, industrial, mining, transportation, utility, and infrastructure projects.
Support environmental aspects of project planning, design, construction, and operational activities.
Review engineering and construction plans for environmental compliance considerations.
Develop environmental compliance plans, permit matrices, environmental commitment tracking systems, and mitigation strategies.
Coordinate environmental field investigations and oversee subcontractors and specialty consultants as appropriate.
Support environmental inspection and monitoring programs during construction.
Serve as a technical liaison with clients, regulatory agencies, contractors, and project stakeholders.
Participate in agency meetings, site visits, compliance inspections, and project coordination meetings.
Respond to agency comments, compliance inquiries, and permit application review requests.
Build and maintain positive working relationships with regulatory agencies, clients, and project stakeholders.
Manage environmental tasks and projects of varying size and complexity, including development of scopes of work, schedules, budgets, and staffing plans.
Monitor project financial performance, schedules, technical quality, and deliverables.
Support proposal preparation, business development initiatives, and client relationship management.
Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior staff and conduct quality reviews of technical work products.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, and conduct while adhering to WSP's Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Studies, Ecology, Biology, Natural Resources, Environmental Engineering, Geography, or a closely related discipline.
5+ years of relevant professional experience in environmental consulting, environmental compliance, permitting, environmental assessment, or environmental management.
Demonstrated experience supporting environmental compliance and/or permitting programs for industrial, energy, mining, construction, infrastructure, transportation, or utility projects.
Working knowledge of applicable environmental laws, regulations, and programs, including:
Clean Water Act (CWA), including Sections 401, 402, and 404
National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)
Endangered Species Act (ESA)
Clean Air Act (CAA)
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA)
Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) requirements
National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) stormwater permitting and compliance
Applicable federal, state, and local environmental permitting frameworks

Experience preparing technical reports, permit applications, environmental compliance documentation, and regulatory correspondence.
Familiarity with GIS applications, environmental data management systems, and/or compliance tracking tools.
Strong technical writing, verbal communication, analytical, and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively both independently and as part of multidisciplinary project teams.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet project deadlines, and maintain high-quality work products.
Ability and willingness to travel throughout the Midwest and conduct field work in varying weather, terrain, and site conditions.
Must be able to pass a background check in accordance with applicable law and company policy.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Natural Resources, Environmental Engineering, or a related discipline.
Experience supporting energy generation, natural gas, mining, industrial manufacturing, renewable energy, transportation, utilities, or major construction projects.
Experience supporting multi-state environmental permitting or compliance programs.
Knowledge of environmental regulations and permitting processes within Midwestern states.
Experience conducting environmental audits, compliance inspections, and corrective action management.
Experience with wetland delineations, aquatic resources, threatened and endangered species assessments, and/or construction environmental compliance.
Professional certification or progress toward a relevant certification such as Certified Environmental Professional (CEP), Certified Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control (CPESC), Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), Certified Wildlife Biologist (CWB), Project Management Professional (PMP), or Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM).
Project management experience, including developing scopes, budgets, schedules, and coordinating multidisciplinary project teams.
Experience preparing proposals, supporting business development activities, and maintaining client relationships.
Existing relationships or experience coordinating with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies throughout the Midwest.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

WSP provides a flexible and agile workplace model while meeting client needs. Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

WSP USA (and all of its U.S. companies) is an Equal Opportunity Employer Race/Age/Color/Religion/Sex/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity/National Origin/Disability or Protected Veteran Status.

The selected candidate must be authorized to work in the United States.

Notice To Third Party Agencies

WSP does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters, employment agencies, or other staffing services. Unsolicited resumes include any resume or hiring document sent to WSP in the absence of a signed Service Agreement where WSP has expressly requested recruitment/staffing services specific to the position at hand. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers or other business leaders, will become the property of WSP and WSP will have the right to hire that candidate without reservation – no fee or other compensation will be owed or paid to the recruiter, employment agency, or other staffing service.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist - Geologist
jobs.description:
Civil & Environmental Consultants, Inc. (CEC) is seeking a Geologist/Environmental Scientist
to join our growing environmental team in our Toledo, OH
(or Wixom, MI) office. This role offers the opportunity to work on a diverse range of projects supporting solid waste, industrial, energy, public sector, and redevelopment clients across the region. You’ll gain hands-on experience in environmental site investigation, compliance, and remediation while continuing to grow your technical skills and progress toward professional licensure.

Responsibilities

Support and execute environmental site investigations, including soil and groundwater sampling and data collection
Participate in Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs) and due diligence projects
Assist with landfill environmental compliance monitoring programs, including sampling, data management, and reporting
Support remediation activities, including source removal and system monitoring
Prepare technical reports, documentation, and regulatory submittals
Assist with SPCC plan development, stormwater permitting, and air compliance support
Coordinate with project teams, contractors, and regulatory agencies to support project objectives
Provide oversight and guidance to junior staff and field activities as needed
Support multiple projects while maintaining quality and schedule expectations

What We Offer

100% employee-owned firm with a path to long-term growth and ownership access within your first year
Competitive compensation with multiple income streams, including paid overtime, performance bonuses, and stock ownership
55% of profits distributed through employee bonuses
A clearly defined career path with mentorship and support toward licensure
Opportunity to work on a diverse project portfolio across multiple industries
Flexible and hybrid work schedule options
Comprehensive benefits starting day one (healthcare, dental, vision), along with a 401(k) with a company match beginning the first of the month following your start date
A collaborative environment that encourages learning, cross-training, and professional development
Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Environmental Science, or related field
3+ years of relevant experience in environmental consulting or related work
GIT certification (or ability to obtain) with interest in pursuing PG licensure is preferred
Experience with environmental site assessments (Phase I/II ESAs) and soil/groundwater investigations
Familiarity with environmental compliance programs, including landfill monitoring and/or SPCC
Experience with Sanitas, Dumpstat, and database management/development a plus
Strong technical writing, data management, and communication skills

We have experts! CEC is consistently ranked as a Top 500 Design Firm and Top 200 Environmental Firm by Engineering News-Record
. We are looking for people who enjoy using their education and experience to solve difficult technical problems and work on interesting projects. You can accomplish this while working with a team of professionals who are equally motivated to provide high levels of service to our clients and to teach you along the way.

We have support! We have a variety of Employee Resource Groups, including CEC Community - focused on giving back to the communities in which we work; CEC Ignite - focused on helping professionals early in their careers to develop their pathway; CEC iDEA - focused on inclusion, diversity, equality, and acceptance; and CEC Women - focused on creating internal and external opportunities for women to network and leverage professional experience!

We care about our people! People and Culture are two of the five elements of our strategic plan. When you care about your people, they will want to grow a career with you - that is our goal. CEC offers you a small-firm work environment with large-firm opportunities. Not only will we help you develop professionally, but we will also provide an opportunity to become an owner of the firm and share in its success.

CEC offers a matching 401(k); profit sharing; a performance bonus; company stock; medical, dental, and vision insurance; short and long-term disability; tuition assistance; professional development; and work-life balance.

CEC is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in recruiting, hiring or promotion based on race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, transgender status), national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status or any other basis or characteristic prohibited by applicable federal, state, or local law.

THIRD PARTY RECRUITERS

If CEC has not expressly requested recruiting services or contractually engaged with you for recruiting services on a specific position, any resumes or candidate profiles sent to CEC shall be considered unsolicited. Therefore, any such submissions will be considered property of CEC, with no associated fees due to your firm.
